Auto-answered by the orchestrator clarify-respond workflow.

DECISIONS:
Q1: A

RATIONALE:
Q1: Each of the eight gate jobs in `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml` already prints `GH_PAT_BUDGET phase=start|end workflow=test-and-mark-stable job=<name> remaining=unknown reset=unknown ...` (for example lines 681 and 3232 for `e2e-smoke-test`). Those lines leave the fields `unknown` only because of the comment at line 678, "no rate_limit read, so the release gate adds no GitHub request". The issue itself points out that `GET /rate_limit` does not use up the allowance, so that reason no longer holds. `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml` (lines 446-460 and 847-861) already fills the same fields from one `gh api rate_limit` read. Using that pattern meets the issue's intent (remaining core allowance and reset time at each job's start and end) with an existing contractual prefix. It adds no duplicate line with overlapping meaning and changes no existing log key (§10). The issue's `GATE_RATE_LIMIT` name was offered only "for example". No test in `tests/` locks the gate's `remaining=unknown` value, so filling it breaks no contract.

EXECUTION PLAN (required for any non-letter decision):
Q1 (option A; plan added because it changes an acceptance criterion and the issue's change 4):
  strategy: derive_from_repo
  inputs:
    - `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml`: the start and end `GH_PAT_BUDGET` steps of the jobs `e2e-smoke-test`, `workflow-log-analysis-test`, `orphan-workflows-test`, `orchestrate-decompose-test`, `validate-standalone-test`, `clarify-rejects-unsolvable-test`, `e2e-alt-model-test` and `validate`. That is 24 `GH_PAT_BUDGET` occurrences in total, including the comment lines.
    - `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml` lines 446-460 (start) and 847-861 (end) as the reference pattern. The start step writes the reading to `GH_PAT_BUDGET_FILE` under `runner.temp`. The end step reads that file to work out `used_in_job`.
  steps:
    - In every gate job, change the start step so it does one `gh api rate_limit --jq '[.resources.core.remaining, .resources.core.reset] | @tsv'` read with the PAT as `GH_TOKEN`. Check the result against `^[0-9]+[[:space:]][0-9]+$`. If it does not match, or the read fails, fall back to `remaining=unknown reset=unknown`. A failed read must never fail the step or the job.
    - Do the same in the end step, and keep the existing `${counter_keys}` suffix. Filling `used_in_job` from a start file the way `review_autofix.yml` does is allowed but not required. If it is not filled, it stays `unknown`.
    - Replace the comment at line 678 ("no rate_limit read ... adds no GitHub request") with one stating that `/rate_limit` does not use up the core allowance. Also update any other comment that says the same thing.
    - Add no `GATE_RATE_LIMIT` prefix and no new stable-log-prefix registry entry. The `agents.d/` or README text for this issue describes the filled `GH_PAT_BUDGET` fields in the gate instead.
    - Add a contract test that checks every gate job has a start and an end `GH_PAT_BUDGET` step that reads `rate_limit` and keeps the `unknown` fallback.
    - Moving these bodies into a shared `scripts/` helper is allowed if it keeps the workflow under the 480,000-byte guard. Step `name:`, `id:`, `if:` and `env:` stay in the workflow.
  replaces_acceptance_criterion: "A gate run prints the `GATE_RATE_LIMIT` line twice per job."
  equivalence_argument: The replacement criterion is "a gate run prints a filled `GH_PAT_BUDGET phase=start|end ... job=<name> remaining=<n> reset=<epoch>` line twice per job, falling back to `unknown` only when the read fails". It records the same data (core remaining and reset epoch) at the same points (job start and end), from the same read that does not use up the allowance. The log analysis that already parses `GH_PAT_BUDGET` gets the numbers without a new parser.
  reversibility: If a separate `GATE_RATE_LIMIT` line is wanted later, it can be added next to the filled lines and reuse the same single read (option C). Nothing in this choice blocks that.

ESCALATION (required for any ESCALATE decision):
None.
